facts.raw_span: progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over the preceding 5 days
no prior medical history
alert (GCS 15), afebrile, and appeared well
both external ear canals were obstructed by effusion and cerumen
routine blood tests were unremarkable
Three-month history of “ear problems”
initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation
bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal
adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening
Brainstem evoked response audiometry demonstrated a threshold of 40 dB with normal wave latencies on the left
80 dB threshold with prolonged wave I latency on the right, indicating profound right-sided hearing loss
no nystagmus

concepts.why: The patient's history of ear problems, otitis media with effusion, and tympanic perforation, along with the current findings of bilateral osteolysis and profound right-sided hearing loss, suggest a diagnosis of cholesteatoma.

The patient's symptoms of progressive unsteadiness, recurrent falls, and hearing loss, along with the findings of bilateral osteolysis and abnormal brainstem evoked response audiometry, suggest a diagnosis of labyrinthitis.
The patient's history of ear problems and initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion, along with the current findings of bilateral osteolysis, suggest a diagnosis of otitis media with effusion.
The patient's findings of bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, along with the presence of adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening, suggest a diagnosis of mastoiditis.
The patient's finding of adenoid hypertrophy, along with the presence of mild sinus mucosal thickening, suggests a diagnosis of adenoid hypertrophy.
The patient's finding of mild sinus mucosal thickening, along with the presence of adenoid hypertrophy, suggests a diagnosis of sinusitis.
The patient's finding of profound right-sided hearing loss, as demonstrated by brainstem evoked response audiometry, suggests a diagnosis of hearing loss.
The patient's symptoms of progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls, along with the findings of abnormal brainstem evoked response audiometry, suggest a diagnosis of vestibular dysfunction.

rationales.F11: Profound right-sided hearing loss is consistent with C01 and C07.
rationales.F12: Absence of nystagmus makes C02 and C08 less likely.
